assessments.method: The pinned report attributes to LOB-Impact a counterfactual benchmark that injects metaorders into five neural limit-order-book generators across five NASDAQ stocks and measures resulting impact exponents.
assessments.claim: The report attributes to the authors exponents between 0.63 and 1.21 and the interpretation that market-impact behaviour emerges from next-token training. Neither the measurements nor the underlying paper were independently verified in this pilot.
assessments.relevance: An impact-response test is potentially more informative for simulator selection than matching marginal order-flow statistics. It could become a screening gate for market-simulation research, not a profitability signal.
assessments.limitations: The reported generator/stock sample is narrow; experimental intervention design, calibration to real execution and sensitivity to order size cannot be evaluated from the report summary. The quoted exponents are author-reported, not measured here.
assessments.falsification: On held-out securities, dates and order sizes, pre-register tolerances for empirical signed impact, temporary-versus-permanent response and uncertainty bands. Reject simulator fidelity if it misses those ranges or materially degrades outside the reported sample.
assessments.title: LOB-Impact Benchmark: Emergent Market Impact in Generative Limit Order Book Models

assessments.method: The pinned report describes a Neural Filter Estimator that amortises Bayesian filtering into a forward pass that produces a posterior distribution over latent statistical-arbitrage spread states.
assessments.claim: The report attributes to the authors controlled calibration evidence and Korean-equity results relative to point estimates and an Attention Factor Model. These are unreplicated, source-reported outcomes rather than demonstrated transferable performance.
assessments.relevance: Posterior-aware decisions may offer an explicit way to study forecast uncertainty, risk limits and position sizing instead of depending on a single estimated state.
assessments.limitations: No independent posterior calibration checks, chronological leakage audit, baseline parity review or transaction-cost sensitivity analysis was performed. Korean-equity evidence alone does not establish out-of-market calibration or net profitability.
assessments.falsification: Compare NFE with a matched point estimator and a simple probabilistic filter on purged chronological splits. Pre-register coverage, PIT uniformity, CRPS, log score, cost-aware outcomes and regime breakdowns; reject the added complexity if calibration or performance is not robust.
assessments.title: Amortized Neural Filtering for Calibrated Posteriors in Statistical Arbitrage

assessments.method: The pinned report describes Rachev-ratio portfolio optimisation using TimeGAN scenarios, comparing synthetic replacement and supplementation of historical return samples across twelve ETFs.
assessments.claim: The report attributes to the authors underestimation of volatility and tail dependence in synthetic scenarios, without a causal performance improvement over historical resampling. The original empirical outputs were not inspected.
assessments.relevance: Tail-sensitive portfolio objectives can magnify shortcomings of synthetic data; this provides a useful candidate negative-control case before adding synthetic scenarios to risk research.
assessments.limitations: The abstract-level record does not expose the scenario-generation protocol, conditioning, effective sample size, uncertainty of tail estimates or alternative generators. No portfolio returns or tail-risk metrics were recomputed.
assessments.falsification: Using purged rolling windows, compare historical-only, synthetic-only and supplement scenarios on out-of-sample upper/lower tail dependence, exceedance calibration, turnover and drawdown. Reject supplementation if tail-risk estimation or stability worsens.
assessments.title: Rachev-Ratio Portfolio Optimization with TimeGAN Scenarios: Replacement versus Supplementation
